context: This portion of the list is n0 (1) → P (0) → n1 (3) → …. Given predecessor n0, the goal is to remove P. Node n0 need not be the head of the entire list.
description: The figure has two panels, one above the other. After removal, P and its arrow to n1 are drawn with dashed lines for comparison. The figure does not show memory being freed.
prose.result: Given predecessor n0, redirecting one reference takes O(1) time and leaves the other nodes in place. This step excludes the time needed to find the predecessor.

steps.announcement: Before removal, n0, P, and n1 are linked in that order, ready to bypass P.
steps.explanation: The links are n0 (1) → P (0) → n1 (3) → …. Since n0.next points to P and P.next points to n1, the path from n0 to n1 must pass through P. The next step redirects n0.next.
steps.key_state: Before removal, n0 → P → n1, so P is reachable from n0.
steps.title: Before removal: n0 → P → n1

steps.announcement: Point n0.next directly to n1. Node P is now unreachable from the list, completing the removal.
steps.explanation: Execute n0.next = n1. The main chain becomes n0 (1) → n1 (3) → …. Node P (0) still points to n1 through next, but it is no longer reachable by following the list from the head through n0. Logical removal is complete.
steps.key_state: With n0.next = n1, the main chain becomes n0 → n1. Node P is unreachable but still points to n1.
steps.title: Redirect the reference: n0.next = n1

prose.summary: Change the predecessor's next reference to bypass the node being removed.
prose.title: Removing a node from a linked list
